title: EVDMARL: Efficient Value Decomposition-based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Domain-Randomization for Complex Analog Circuit Design Migration
problem: Automated analog circuit design migration under various operating conditions requires excessive iterations of costly simulations to converge. Conventional approaches model this as black-box optimization without leveraging transfer learning capabilities.
motivation: Automating circuit design migration significantly alleviates designer burden and enables efficient generation of circuits meeting specifications under new operating conditions with minimal manual effort.
method: The framework solves complex circuit design by breaking it into smaller independent problems, with one learner assigned to each sub-circuit component (called value decomposition-based multi-agent learning). During training, the system varies the operating conditions extensively (domain randomization), teaching the system to recognize design patterns that work across different scenarios. This enables the system to automatically adapt circuit designs to new operating conditions with minimal additional costly simulations, eliminating the need for engineers to manually specify how each circuit component should change.
key_novelty: Using multiple learners trained on randomly varied conditions (value decomposition-based multi-agent learning with domain randomization) allows circuit designs to automatically adapt to new operating scenarios without manual redesign.
contributions: Novel value decomposition-based multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for complex analog circuit design
Eliminates manual specification of sub-circuits for new operating conditions
Incorporates domain randomization for robust generalization to unseen scenarios
Demonstrates faster convergence than state-of-the-art methods with fewer simulation iterations

metrics.accuracy: meets circuit specifications under new operating conditions

primary_theme: Automated analog circuit design migration via multi-agent RL
